display.purpose: The song title only. Geist 700, -0.035em, balanced wrap.

headline.purpose: The next song title in the up-next row.

title.purpose: Setlist name at the head of the rail and the sheet.

lyrics.purpose: Lyrics at regular 400, user-sized in five steps: 1rem, 1.125rem (default), 1.375rem, 1.625rem, 2rem; size changes animate 260ms.

chord.purpose: Chord symbols over their word, in the chord colour; superscripts at 0.68em. Accidentals spelled b and #.

mono.purpose: Geist Mono for musical data and numbers only: row numbers and keys, the key chip; at other sizes the key name, offset, key grid, notation segment, keycaps, dock count and up-next key.

subtitle.purpose: The artist line under the song title, in ink-2.

body.purpose: Base text at regular 400; no weight lighter than 400.

ui-strong.purpose: Bar titles, the current song-row title, the dock song name, the toast.

label.purpose: Geist control labels: segment options, Sign in, menu rows (Aa at 0.9375rem). Centred in their controls with no padding offset.

caption.purpose: Dates, meta, the Key and Up next captions, song details, popover headings (600, ink-2).

section-label.purpose: Song section names only (Verse, Chorus), uppercase, led by a 6px square pixel. Never a decorative eyebrow.

shadows.name: pixel-now-glow
shadows.purpose: Current song pixel in the strip.

motion.name: ease-liquid
motion.purpose: Anything glass that moves or scales: presses, the segmented thumb, panels, the toast, switches.

motion.name: thumb
motion.purpose: Segmented thumb translateX and width; placed without animation the first time.

motion.name: panel
motion.value: open 480ms ease-liquid from translateY(18px) scale(0.96); close 420ms
motion.purpose: Bottom sheets on phones; popovers on wide screens grow from their trigger.

motion.name: reduced
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: every transition and animation; scrolling jumps.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: Setlist sidebar (or a full-width set row under the top row), chord settings in the top row, split songs with equal panes (or one song in two lyric columns); hides the progress segments and bottom row.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Top row (Lyrics | Chords, share), progress segments, bottom row (Aa, Up next, key), panels as bottom sheets.

ground.layer: position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 0; pointer-events: none
ground.note: One even field with a single soft wash of light from the top. No radial glows, textures or decorative pixels in the ground.

glassEngine.technique: Hybrid: CSS backdrop-filter stack everywhere; Chromium-only bezel refraction via size-specific SVG displacement maps.
glassEngine.frosted: blur(var(--glass-blur, 14px)) saturate(185%) brightness(1.04); 24px for sheets and popovers

refraction.bezelDefault: round(radius * 0.6), clamped 1-18 and radius - 1; skip radius < 3
cacheKeys: width x height x radius x bezel x blur (filter)
refraction.specular: map over 2.5x bezel, light at 60deg, alpha slope 0.55, saturate 1.8

glassEngine.refractionBlur: data-blur 3 for floating groups and the sidebar, 6 for the toast and TV controls, 8 for sheets and popovers
glassEngine.grouping: No full-width bars: each group of related controls is its own capsule (48px top, 56px bottom); the rows holding them have no glass and pass clicks through.
glassEngine.contrast: prefers-contrast: more makes neutral tints near-opaque (0.95-0.97 alpha) and strengthens ink-2, ink-3, hairline, rim-edge, fill-on and pixel-off.

pixelStates.played: var(--pixel-played): white at 0.52 (black at 0.45 in light), songs already played and the end-of-set row
pixelStates.now: var(--pixel-on): the accent; on the phone progress segments it adds 0 1px 8px var(--pixel-glow)
pixelStates.shapes: 4px progress segments (22 x 4px on the TV), 10px row pixels, 8px end-of-set pixels

fonts.ui: Geist 400/500/600/700: every word, controls included; 400 lyrics and body, 600 labels and UI strong, 700 song titles at -0.035em. Stack: 'Geist', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'PingFang TC', 'Noto Sans TC', 'Microsoft JhengHei', sans-serif.
fonts.mono: Geist Mono 500/600/700: musical data and numbers only (chords, key names, offsets, key grid, the 1 4 5 / A B C segment, row numbers and keys, counts, steppers, keycaps). Stack: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'PingFang TC', 'Noto Sans TC', monospace.
fonts.accidentals: Spelled b and #; neither face has the flat or sharp glyph.
fonts.productionRequirement: Self-host both families; the Google Fonts CDN link in the mock is not part of the system.

opticalAlignment.capCentre: Geist and Geist Mono centre their capitals in the line box (cap 0.71em, ascent 1.01em, descent 0.29em).
opticalAlignment.controlLabels: No padding offset: labels centre in fixed-height controls by the box alone.
opticalAlignment.titleInfoButton: margin-top: calc(var(--title-size) * 0.54 - 20px) centres the 40px info button on the title's first line (1.08 line height).
opticalAlignment.tolerance: Measured in the browser: info icon within 0.1px of the title cap height, labels within about 0.5px of their control centre. Re-measure after changing a font, size or control height.

icons.size: var(--icon): 24px at 1x; 18px at min-resolution 2dppx; 20px at min-resolution 2.5dppx
icons.reason: Each icon pixel is two grid units, so it spans 2 device px at 1x, 3 at 2x and 5 at 3x.
icons.mark: Pixel cross drawn at 20px in a 32px box, in chord, independent of --icon

extensions.status: Recorded from the public setlist view design mock (.impeccable/mocks/praise-room-public-setlist-view.html), the only implementation. ui/ has not adopted this world; ui/src/styles.css still carries the provisional navy palette being replaced.

accent.derived: chord and pixel-on = accent; fill-on = accent at 32% (14% light); pixel-glow = accent at 80% (40% light); c1 = accent

narrative.northStar: The Set as a Strip of Light
narrative.overview:
The song owns the screen. The controls float above it as separate pieces of liquid glass, grouped by what they do, with no full-width bar behind them. The palette is black and white with one accent, electric blue: pure black ground (white in the light theme), hue-free greys, and blue only where something is lit. The set is drawn as a strip of square pixels, one per song: songs still to come are dark, played songs are half-lit white, and the current song is lit in electric blue and glowing. On phones the strip is a row of thin segments under the top controls. On wide screens it is the pixel beside each song in the sidebar, and on a TV it runs along the foot of the screen.

The density is that of a reading instrument. On a phone the lyrics run in one column of up to 760px. On wide screens two songs stand side by side: the current one and the next, ready to slide over. Reading text never sits on glass or a card. Content dissolves into a scroll-edge band before it reaches the floating controls. Dark is the default theme, for dim rooms and stages. The light theme has the same structure, on white, with a deeper blue.

Two materials carry the brand. The first is the pixel, sharp and square: the smallest unit of light. The second is liquid glass: round, rimmed, refracting, and springy in motion. Pixels are never rounded. Glass is never square.

The layout follows Apple's Liquid Glass guidance (developer.apple.com, "Adopting Liquid Glass"). Glass is the navigation layer above the content. Related controls share one piece of glass, and unrelated ones float apart. Nested shapes are concentric. The page works with reduced transparency, increased contrast and reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Black, white and hue-free greys, with one accent (`--accent`, electric blue). Colour chords, an opt-in reading aid, is the only other colour.
Controls float as glass groups; the reading surface is bare ground.
Every essential control a phone player needs mid-song is in the bottom row, in thumb reach.
Square pixels mark the set, sections, the original key, pins and the brand mark. A pixel's state is told by brightness alone: off, played, on.
Pixelarticons (MIT) are drawn at the `--icon` size (24px at 1x, 18px at 2x, 20px at 2.5x and up) with `shape-rendering: crispEdges`.
Motion uses two curves: a calm ease-out for colour and fades, and a liquid overshoot for anything that moves like glass.
Geist sets every word, controls included. Geist Mono sets musical data and numbers only. Both fall back to PingFang TC and Noto Sans TC for 繁體中文.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Black, white and hue-free greys carry the interface; one accent, `--accent`, lights what matters (chords, the current song, selection, focus). Every coloured token derives from `--accent`, never from a hue of its own. No song, section or state gets a colour of its own. Colour chords is the one, opt-in exception, and it touches chord text alone.

rules.name: The Light by State Rule
rules.body: A set pixel tells where a song sits in the set by brightness alone: dark (`pixel-off`) to come, half-lit (`pixel-played`) played, lit (`pixel-on`, glowing on the phone's segments) now.

rules.name: The Chord Carries the Light Rule
rules.body: `chord` (the accent) is the only saturated text colour by default. Labels sit a step quieter. Body text, titles and controls stay in ink.

rules.name: The One Sans Rule
rules.body: Geist sets every word: titles, lyrics, artist, setlist names, song titles, meta, and every control label. Lyrics and body are regular 400; song titles are 700. Weight and size make the hierarchy; don't add a second sans, a display family, or a Light weight.

rules.name: The Mono Is Music Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono sets musical data and numbers only: chords, key names, offsets, the key grid, the 1 4 5 / A B C segment, row numbers and keys, counts, steppers and keycaps. Never use it for a control's word label, prose, headings, section names, or song titles. Accidentals are spelled `b` and `#` (`Bb`, `F#m`), because neither face has ♭ or ♯ glyphs and a fallback glyph would break the monospace rhythm.

rules.name: The Optical Centre Rule
rules.body: Geist and Geist Mono centre their capitals in the line box, so labels centre in fixed-height controls with no padding nudge. The title's info button centres on the title's first line: `margin-top: calc(var(--title-size) * 0.54 - 20px)`. Measure again before changing a font, size or control height.

rules.name: The Song Owns the Screen Rule
rules.body: The lyrics start above the fold at 390px. Chrome floats; nothing pushes the song down except the title, artist, chord controls and section chips.

rules.name: The Thumb Rule
rules.body: On a phone, everything a player reaches for mid-song (text size, the next song, the key) is in the bottom row. The top holds only what is set once.

rules.name: The Glass Floats Rule
rules.body: Only the navigation layer is glass: the floating control groups, the sidebar, sheets, popovers, the toast and the auto-scroll pill. Lyrics, titles, the set name and the split panes sit on bare ground.

rules.name: The Group, Don't Bar Rule
rules.body: There is no full-width bar. Related controls share one piece of glass (Lyrics | Chords; ‹ Up next ›), and unrelated controls float apart, 6–8px from each other. The rows that hold them have no glass and let clicks through.

rules.name: The No Glass-in-Glass Rule
rules.body: Glass never sits on glass. Controls inside a glass group or panel are plain fills (`fill-hover`, `fill-press`, `fill-on`) or bare taps.

rules.name: The Denser Over Motion Rule
rules.body: Glass over moving lyrics (the bottom groups and the auto-scroll pill) uses `glass-tint-over`, so its own labels always win.

rules.name: The Concentric Rule
rules.body:
A shape nested in another keeps the same centre of curvature: inner radius = outer radius − inset.
- A 48px top capsule (24px) holds 42px segment buttons 3px in (21px).
- A 56px bottom capsule (28px) holds 44px controls 6px in (22px).
- A 32px sheet with 16px padding holds 16px rows.
- A 24px sidebar with 10px padding holds 14px rows.

rules.name: The Square Pixel Rule
rules.body: A pixel is never rounded, never blurred into a dot, and never drawn at a size where it spans a fractional number of device pixels. Icons take `--icon`, never a fixed size.

dos: **Do** keep neutrals hue-free (`oklch(L 0 0)`) and derive every coloured token from `--accent`.
**Do** float controls as glass groups: put related controls in one capsule, keep unrelated ones apart, and leave the rows that hold them clear.
**Do** keep nested corners concentric: inner radius = outer radius − inset.
**Do** keep everything a phone player needs mid-song in the bottom row, and open panels from the control that triggered them.
**Do** show a set pixel's state by brightness: `pixel-off` to come, `pixel-played` played, `pixel-on` now.

**Do** build glass as a hybrid: the CSS backdrop-filter stack everywhere, with bezel refraction from size-cached SVG maps in Chromium. Honour reduced transparency, increased contrast and forced colours.
**Do** draw pixelarticons (MIT) at `var(--icon)`, with `fill="currentColor"` and `shape-rendering: crispEdges`.
**Do** set every word in Geist, controls included; keep Geist Mono for chords, keys, offsets, counts, row numbers, steppers, keycaps and the notation segment.
**Do** self-host Geist (400/500/600/700) and Geist Mono (500/600/700) in production, keeping the PingFang TC / Noto Sans TC fallbacks for 繁體中文.
**Do** keep tap targets at least 40px, and 44px or more for rows, key cells and standalone glass controls.
**Do** dissolve content into a scroll-edge band before it reaches floating controls.
donts: **Don't** give songs, sections or states their own colour, tint the greys, or let colour chords tint anything but chord text.
**Don't** put a full-width glass bar behind controls, or join unrelated controls in one piece of glass.
**Don't** put lyrics, titles or reading text inside glass, or in a bordered sheet or card.
**Don't** nest glass inside glass. Controls inside glass are fills.
**Don't** show the next song's lyrics below the current song on a phone; Up next names it instead.
**Don't** dim one of the split songs or call one "now" and the other "next"; both are read at once.

**Don't** hide the setlist on wide screens; fold it into the set row. Don't squeeze it into the top row either: there the titles don't fit, and showing only the songs already on screen repeats the panes.
**Don't** round a pixel, or replace a square pixel with a dot.
**Don't** draw icons at a fixed size, or use any icon set other than pixelarticons.
**Don't** set control labels, prose, headings, section names or song titles in Geist Mono, or use a Light weight for lyrics.
**Don't** use the section-label style (uppercase, 0.12em tracking) for anything but song section names.
**Don't** implement glass with WebGL or SVG-only filters, or recompute refraction maps every frame.
**Don't** reuse the old navy palette from `ui/src/styles.css`, or the retired ink-blue tokens.
